title: Residential proximity to intensive animal agriculture associates with increased prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in homes - Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology
description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR), a global public health threat, affects rural communities disproportionately due to their unique regional exposures, including proximity to animal feeding operations (AFOs), a source of AMR genes. We evaluated residential proximity to AFOs and the presence of AMR genes in the home dust resistome, the collection of antimicrobial resistant genes within a microbial community. We conducted metagenomic sequencing of 534 bedroom dust samples to characterize the resistome for a subset of homes of Iowa participants in the US Agricultural Health Study. We examined the association between the presence of AMR genes in dust samples and the total number of AFOs and distance-weighted number of livestock animal units (AUs) within 2, 5, and 10 km of participant homes, using data from the Iowa Department of Natural Resources. Homes that were closer to a greater number of AFOs and AUs had increased odds of the presence of AMR genes in the dust, including genes resistant to multiple classes of antimicrobials. We found that AFOs were positively related to the composition of the indoor home dust resistome, which may serve as a potential environmental reservoir of antimicrobial resistance with implications for the health of household occupants.

The head of the Environmental Protection Agency has announced plans for sweeping rollbacks to Biden-era oil and gas regulations aimed at reducing emissions of methane and other greenhouse gases.

EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin made the announcement Wednesday during the annual New Mexico Oil and Gas Association conference, held at the Santa Fe Community Convention Center as environmental advocates protested along the sidewalk.

“If you take one message away from today, know that the Trump EPA is listening and is responding,” Zeldin said speaking, to a room full of industry figures.

Nini Gu, senior regulatory and legislative manager for the Environmental Defense Fund, said in an interview these rollbacks are “the last thing that should happen” to address pollution from the oil and gas industry.
